Chess GrandMaster Kenny Solomon

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Kenny Solomon

Kenny Solomon, 33 has become South Africa’s first chess grandmaster after winning the Africa individual chess championship in Namibia in December. He is only the second grandmaster in sub-Saharan Africa after Amon Simutowe of Zambia.

Kenny Solomon is one of 8 children and started playing chess as a 13-year-old in Mitchells Plain, after his older brother was flown to the Philippines to take part in a Chess Olympiad. He read a book about former world champion Anatoly Karpov, taught himself to play and won the under-16 national championship two years later.

Mitchell’s plain is known for it’s gang violence and drug abuse, his web site says that he was exposed to gang culture from an early age. He realized quite tactically at a young age that if he did not create his own future he may be caught up in the violence of the area.

But chess kept him away from these influences, their conflict was contained not in turf war but the 8 x 8 square of their chess board. Frins would gather in their back yard near the washing line and play blitz tournaments whenever they could.

In 2011 Solomon married an Italian chess player and moved to Venice, where he competes on the European circuit. A year later, a strong performance at the World Chess Olympiad gave him the status of grandmaster-elect.
He told South Africa’s Daily Maverick: “There are many ingredients to make one a good chess player – talent, hard work, etc. In my case, it’s dedication, determination and perseverance. As a youngster there were not too many opportunities, but I didn’t give up.”

He hopes to play chess professionally for another 10 or 15 years, he added. “If I didn’t play chess, what would I have been? I don’t know. I chose my profession at age 13.”

“Four Corners” is a new South African movie about a boy on the Cape Flats who has to choose between gangsterism and chess playing. It loosely mirrors Kenny’s life and he was the script advisor in this movie.
Kenny has also taught chess to the inmates at Pollsmoor prison.

I have made contact with the makers of Four Corners and they seem quite amenable to allowing us to use some of their footage. I am also looking for footage on his win in Namibia.

The Chess Federation of South Africa is apparently going to fly him out soon for an award ceremony. I am going to get hold of their president to get the timing of this.

Press Release:


SA’s Chess Grandmaster
From humble origins on the Cape Flats, 33-year-old Kenny Solomon has become a god in the international chess world. Carte Blanche catches up with South Africa’s first chess grandmaster at his home in Mitchells Plain to hear how he decided against the conflict waged in the area’s gangland turf wars in exchange for the infinite battlefields of the chess board.


Script:


Kenny Solomon Script

Kenny
“You have to introduce your weapons.”

V/O
They say that “Life is like a game of Chess, to win you have to move”.

And Kenny Solomon is the man with all the moves, he say’s that chess was his salvation when he started playing it as a youngster.

Kenny
“That’s when I found my treasure and chess became my world. That’s when I got sucked into the game and chess became my drug you know.”

V/O
And Kenny Solomon is on a high, he has just been awarded the title of South Africa’s first chess Grandmaster. This is the highest title a chess player can achieve globally and it is awarded for life by the World Chess Federation. Grandmasters are the gods/rock stars of the international chess world.

John
“You must have been absolutely elated at that point.”

Kenny
“I was over the moon. I had a sense of accomplishment and fulfilment and it is a goal that I have been pursuing for 22 years to achieve. It’s been quite a journey.”

Excerpt from Four Corners

“This is the battle ground, each soldier has a different battle to fight, the queen is strong, like our mothers are strong, she moves fast don’t mess with her.”

V/O
Four Corners is a South African movie set on the Cape Flats, it is a story about a young chess player and the life and death decisions he has to make growing up in the marginalised community of the Cape Flats, known as one of the most violent areas in South
Africa.

Up Sound

“The Knight he comes from far and he kills at close quarters,. Checkmate.’

V/O
There are many similarities with Kenny’s childhood, and he contributed to the making of the film when he served as the chess script supervisor while the script was still in development.


V/O
Kenny was born on the Cape Flats 35 years ago and like the character in Four Corners, the game of chess shaped his life.

Kenny
“This is where I grew up, and I played everyday with my friends and it brings back a lot of memories, we used to play marbles here, it’s been a long time. So this was my childhood.”

V/O
Kenny is one of 8 children, and all of his siblings played and loved chess, he says that although he learnt to play the game at the age of 7, it didn’t capture his imagination then.

Kenny
“I didn’t like chess, it wasn’t interesting. When you are a kid and you have so much energy, I had to be outside with my friends.”

V/O
He changed his mind when he was 13 years old and his brother Maxwell was chosen to go overseas to play at the Chess Olympiad in the Philippines in 1992.

Kenny
“I saw my brother off at the airport with my whole family, and I was inspired by this and I got home and took a chess book off the shelf and started to study the games of Anatoly Karpov and this was how I got into chess.”

V/O
Maxwell took his brother under his wing and within two years Kenny was the South Africa’s Under-16 champion.

Maxwell
“I just came from the Olympic the other day and I helped the guy, especially when you helped the guy, and now the guy beats you.”

John
“The student was becoming the master, as they say.”

Maxwell
“I thought it would take longer, it was so quick , it was so quick.”

Link
Kenny says that there is no doubt that playing chess improved his concentration at school and there is scientific evidence that it has benefits in other areas too, including raising IQ increasing concentration and improving creativity.

Up Sound “Settle down”

V/O
Like the character in Four Corners , chess kept Kenny and his brothers off the streets, preferring to stay at home and play indoors.

Up Sound Four Corners

“Dominate the board and it’s position. Be the chess player and not the chess piece.”

V/O
Chess literally turned Kenny’s life around.

John
“You were quite naughty boy back then?”

Kenny
“I was very naughty. I was stealing in shops. I was fighting with my friends against other groups. Once you are in it is difficult to get out of it and chess pulled me out of it.”

John
“As a mother, were you happy that it was a game that kept them off the streets.”
Rose
“Yes, of course because they were indoors in the house.”

John
“For people who don’t live in the area, was it as obvious as that , did you see gansters prowling the streets, did you see violence on a day to day basis?”

Maxwell
“It’s there, its right there, you don’t have to go and search it could flare up at any moment.

Four Corners brick through window

V/O
In a recent survey Cape Town was voted the most violent city in the whole of Africa. The high murder rates were largely attributed to the Cape Flats, where gangsterism is rife. In Four Corners , the chess player makes a decision to join one of the warring gangs with violent consequences. Like any good chess player, Kenny strategically realized that he had to charter a new path for himself or he would become a pawn trapped in the violent web of gangsterism.

Up sound “Ricardo go home”

Kenny
“This is the gate of Lentegeur High, and this is the high school that I have attended in my high school years and as you can see, the school has changed over the years and it more or less resembles a prison.”

Kenny
“My first day at Lentegeur High, I saw another student and he was running for his life and there was a gangster who came onto the school with a knife, and the guys knife went into the fence, he narrowly escaped and it was an example of some of the things we shouldn’t be seeing, and it shouldn’t be happening on our schools.’

Excerpt Four Corners
“ What is this? Chess is life?”
“It’s the king, the king lives forever.”
“Nothing’s forever.”

“The King is, nothing can take him off the board.”

V/O
And nothing could stop Kenny. His tenacious commitment to studying and analysing games from past Grand Masters allowed him to excel.

Kenny
“It was like I discovered a treasure once I opened a chess book, and I couldn’t wait to finish school and open the chess books and start learning. And immediately my goal was to become a grandmaster. South Africa in its history did not have any grandmasters, I thought to myself, why shouldn’t I try and become a grand master.”

John
“Rose, once he decided to pursue a chess career were you fully behind it?”

Rose
“Of course, and my husband was fully behind him and my husband said to me. Once you are going to see he is going to be a grandmaster, I can see it. He’s take it very, very serious the game.”

V/O
But it has not been an easy road for Kenny. With very little sponsorship for the sport in South Africa, he moved to Venice where he married his Italian wife who is also a chess player and they now have a young daughter. Here he was able to make a modest living by teaching chess and participating in the European Chess Circuit to improve his ratings. This extreme focus paid off.

Link
Kenny Solomon is South Africa’s first chess grandmaster and that makes him a member of an elite club of 1600 of the best chessplayers in the world. An accolade he received after winning the African Championships late last year.

V/O
Eldo Smart is the president of the Chess South Africa.

John
“Put Kenny’s achievement into perspective for us, how big a deal is it?”

Eldo
“This is huge, it’s monumental. It’s like a knighthood that is bestowed upon you and in a world of about 6 billion people to have 1600 only and one guy from Mitchell’s Plain, I think is really really special.”

V/O
Kenny came back to South Africa recently to celebrate his win and receive a Protea Blazer to honour his tremendous achievement.

Kenny
“It’s not talent, that was the main ingredient to my success in chess, its my perseverance and my passion for the game.”

Maxwell
“ I never thought he’d be the first to actually accomplish this goal, its one thing to support someone, its another thing to see it happen. Fantastic.”


Promo 1 - 10 secs

V/O
From Mitchell’s Plain, Kenny Solomon is South Africa’s First Chess Grandmaster.
“It’s taken me 22 years to achieve this, its been quite a journey”.

Promo 2 - 15 secs

V/O
Kenny Solomon from Mitchell’s Plain is South Africa’s first chess grandmaster. As one of only 1600 in the world, it’s an impressive achievement by anyone’s standards.

Promo 3 – 15 seconds

Kenny Solomon is South Africa’s first chess grandmaster and that makes him a member of an elite club of 1600 of the best chessplayers in the world. An accolade he received after winning the African Championships late last year.
